rules.threshold_text: 25 MW monthly maximum demand (the Commission's definition of a large load customer in Order No. 10829)

rules.utility: East Kentucky Power Cooperative, Inc. (EKPC), with its 16 owner-member distribution cooperatives
rules.threshold_text: Data centers (including cryptocurrency mining) with expected or actual peak demand of 15,000 kW (15 MW) or more and a monthly load factor of 60 percent or more, aggregated across co-located and grouped facilities of the same customer; above 250,000 kW (250 MW) a Dedicated Resource is required unless EKPC determines otherwise in its sole discretion
rules.contract_term: Initial term length and renewal periods set in each special contract approved by the PSC; the load ramp schedule may not exceed 5 years
rules.collateral: Cash Pre-Payment Deposit equal to a rolling 6 months of expected maximum monthly billings (after 2 years it may be revised, but never below 2 months), replenished within 7 days of a draw; if the customer is not Creditworthy (at least A- or A3 and liquidity above 20 times the amount), additional collateral equal to 18 months of expected maximum monthly billings; further collateral for PJM capacity or planning reserve commitments and for termination damages; a parent guarantee may cover at most 50 percent (guarantor A+ or A1 or higher), 25 percent (A- or A3 or higher) or 0 percent (BBB+ or Baa1 or lower) of the additional requirement. Build-Out Costs (transmission, distribution and EKPC-supplied dedicated resources) are paid up front as a prepayment
rules.exit_fee: If the agreements terminate or expire before full recovery of Build-Out Costs, the customer pays EKPC and the cooperative any unreimbursed Build-Out Costs, including costs to terminate or settle underlying agreements; the Pre-Payment Deposit may be drawn for damages from early termination
rules.study_timeline: Application with a non-refundable fee of 75,000 USD plus 1,000 USD per MW of final expected load over 15 MW, up to 250,000 USD (the applicant also bears Load Study costs above the fee); Load Study requested from PJM within a commercially reasonable time, no fixed duration; EKPC aims (an objective, not an obligation) to develop a resource plan within 180 days of the application; the customer signs the agreements within 60 days of receipt, and EKPC aims to file them with the PSC within 10 business days

rules.threshold_text: 150 MW (new customers with contract demands of at least 150 MW, or existing customers adding 150 MW or more of incremental load)
rules.contract_term: Initial period of 20 years; at least five years' written notice to discontinue (not reducing the 20-year term); five years' notice to reduce contract capacity, by no more than 20% except by mutual agreement, not given in the first five years
rules.collateral: 24 times the previous maximum monthly non-fuel bill (the maximum expected bill in the first contract year), recomputed annually and updated if 10% greater
rules.exit_fee: On a permanent closure after the first five years of the initial term, a one-time payment equal to five years of minimum billing

rules.utility: Baltimore Gas and Electric Company; Potomac Electric Power Company; Delmarva Power & Light Company (Maryland); and Maryland's other electric companies
rules.threshold_text: large load customer as defined in Public Utilities Article 4-212(a) (now 7-232): aggregate monthly demand of at least 25 MW and a load factor of more than 60 percent; the specific rate schedule applies to more than 25 MW monthly maximum demand at a single location or more than 25 MW aggregated contract capacity in the company's territory (Chapter 353 of 2026, the Utility RELIEF Act)
rules.contract_term: after the initial contract, the customer may terminate on at least 1 year's written notice, and must give at least 1 year's written notice of a contract capacity adjustment, unless a tariff schedule or later contract says otherwise; terminations and adjustments otherwise follow the company's tariff and service contract
rules.collateral: the company may require one or more of: a letter of credit from a financial institution with investment-grade credit metrics; a performance bond from a third-party issuer with investment-grade credit metrics; a corporate guarantee from a parent company with an investment-grade credit rating; or cash
rules.study_timeline: completeness determination within 30 calendar days of a load study request; the customer cures a deficiency within 10 business days; the company completes the load study and reports not later than 18 months after the load study agreement is executed and payment received; extensions by mutual agreement or, for good cause, on request to the Commission

rules.utility: Public Service Electric and Gas Company (PSE&G)
rules.threshold_text: no MW threshold printed for data center requests; the Capacity Review fee is $10,000 instead of $25,000 for requests at 26 kV of less than 20 MW; the FAR and TEA path is for service at 69 kV or higher
rules.contract_term: 26 kV: Electric Service Obligation / Refunding Agreement with refunds of the deposit tied to revenue milestones over a 10-year term; no term printed for the TEA
rules.collateral: Capacity Review: $25,000 fee ($10,000 at 26 kV below 20 MW), non-refundable. FAR: customer commits to a payment of about $400K to $1M+, which serves as a deposit. TEA: customer deposit covering the full cost of construction (typically $40M+). 26 kV: deposit based on construction cost, refundable against revenue milestones
rules.exit_fee: FAR payment: if the project does not continue, actual study costs are retained; the Capacity Review fee is non-refundable

rules.utility: Public Service Electric and Gas Company; Jersey Central Power & Light Company; Atlantic City Electric Company; Rockland Electric Company (New Jersey's electric public utilities)
rules.threshold_text: set by the BPU for each utility at not greater than 50 MW; data centers under common ownership or control, on the same or contiguous sites, or sharing substantial infrastructure are aggregated and treated as one large data center
rules.contract_term: 10-year period from when service commences for the 85 percent payment guarantee and the security (or as otherwise determined in the BPU's standards); no contract term otherwise printed
rules.collateral: deposits, financial security or, for large data center customers with sufficiently high credit ratings, financial commitments, in forms the BPU approves, sufficient to protect ratepayers against a material rate increase should the customer cease operations or take less service than anticipated over the 10-year period
rules.exit_fee: no exit fee printed; the BPU may approve a stranded cost recovery mechanism applicable only to the large data center customer class, for costs not covered by the deposits, security or commitments

rules.utility: Buckeye Power, Inc. and Ohio's Electric Cooperatives (the 24 Ohio distribution cooperatives Buckeye serves)

rules.threshold_text: 25 MW: Schedule DCT applies to data center ESAs signed after the effective date for new load or expansion greater in the aggregate than 25 MW
rules.contract_term: Initial term equal to the Load Ramp Period (no greater than four years) plus eight years
rules.collateral: For customers below A-/A3 ratings, a parent guarantee or collateral (letter of credit or cash) equal to 50 percent of the customer's minimum charges under the ESA; the Commission's modification lets the customer's financial sponsor meet it as a co-signer
rules.exit_fee: Exit fee payable only after five contract years excluding the load ramp period (with a three-year ramp, after year eight); exit fee and collateral revenue to flow back to retail customers
rules.study_timeline: Load study fee of $10k to $100k paid within 45 days; reasonable efforts to complete the load study within 60 days if regional transmission upgrades are needed, otherwise 45 days; 60 days to sign the LOA and ESA

rules.threshold_text: 50 MW or more peak demand at a single facility, or at least 75 MW in the aggregate among the customer's facilities served at 69 kV or above within a 10-mile radius; data center customers served from lines of 69,000 volts or higher that commenced service on or after 1 October 2025 (a single facility of 50 to 75 MW causing no transmission network upgrade costs may be moved to Rate LP-5 by Commission petition)
rules.contract_term: Electric Service Agreement with an initial term of not less than 10 years; initial load ramp schedule for up to the first 5 years of the initial term
rules.collateral: Security equal to the cost of the upgrades needed to serve the customer that are placed in rate base and recovered through transmission rates (the Rate Base Security Obligation), by letter of credit, parent guarantee or other instrument acceptable to the Company; satisfied when transmission revenue from the customer equals that obligation. Contribution in aid of construction as up-front milestone payments for directly assignable transmission and distribution upgrades
rules.exit_fee: The greater of the remaining minimum load guarantee obligation during the ESA term at termination, or the remaining amount of the Rate Base Security Obligation

rules.threshold_text: New or additional separately meterable load of at least 5,000 kW, an average annual load factor of at least 70 percent, served from facilities of 115 kV or greater at 12.5 kV or greater delivery
rules.contract_term: Distribution ESA term negotiable, but structured to recover the full cost of distribution and/or sub-transmission plant investment, maintenance and operation

rules.threshold_text: Large customer: dedicated service capacity of 5 MW or more; a data center is a large customer identified as such during contracting or planning
rules.collateral: Non-refundable deposit at the pre-construction commitment; contribution in aid of construction (CIAC) payments begin at the construction commitment

Non-refundable deposit at the Letter of Authorization; CIAC and milestone payments from the Construction Development Agreement; the ESA is sized to total project cost through fixed capacity and excess facility charges
rules.exit_fee: The member reimburses REC's investments if the project is canceled (from the Construction Development Agreement)

rules.utility: Virginia Electric and Power Company (Dominion Energy Virginia)
rules.threshold_text: Measured or contracted demand of 25 MW or greater on a contiguous site, and a measured or expected load factor of at least 75 percent (demand may be totalized at contiguous locations, not aggregated across accounts, for minimum demands)
rules.contract_term: 14 years, for customers taking initial service and signing an ESA on or after 1 January 2027, the term including any load ramp period of up to four years; during the term contracted capacity may be reduced by up to 20 percent at no cost and by a further 30 percent if another customer assumes it, each reduction on a separate 36-month notice
rules.collateral: 1.5 million USD per MW, reducible by up to 70 percent on the customer's established credit; third-party guarantees and letters of credit allowed; a share released each year throughout the contract term (the Florida copy's text layer prints the fraction as '1714th', an OCR rendering of the order's one-fourteenth); cash collateral accrues interest while held; applies to customers taking initial service and signing an ESA on or after 1 January 2027
rules.exit_fee: If the customer ceases operations or defaults during the contract term, an exit fee covering any outstanding minimum charges over the remaining contract duration (subject to capacity reassignment)

rules.utility: Virginia Electric and Power Company (Dominion Energy Virginia)
rules.threshold_text: Not stated as a size in the letter, which covers the data center industry. Dominion's 2025 10-K applies the construction-period deposit requirement to 'high load customers', a group its Q3 2026 10-Q revenue table defines as customers in Virginia with actual or anticipated forecast demand of 25 MW or higher and annual load factor of 75 percent or higher
rules.collateral: A 250,000 USD deposit with the ELOA to cover engineering costs; deposits for long-lead time equipment before Dominion orders it, refunded at energization; the ESA assigns collateral; from 2025 high load customers provide commitments including cash deposits during the construction period
rules.exit_fee: If the project is canceled before energization, or the customer does not execute an ESA, the customer reimburses Dominion for the investments made on its behalf; the equipment deposit is kept if the equipment cannot be redeployed to another customer
rules.study_timeline: Engineering study under the ELOA typically 9 to 12 months; after it the customer has 90 days to request a CLOA and another 90 days to execute it, or the project is canceled

rules.utility: Virginia Electric and Power Company (Dominion Energy Virginia)
